x: Commentary on Surah al-Jumu'ah. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Commentary on the saying of the Exalted, Majestic be His praise:
h
Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Almighty, the Wise (1)

. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says: Everything in the seven heavens and everything on the earth among His creation glorifies God and exalts Him, willingly or unwillingly — the Sovereign, the Holy, to whom belongs the dominion of this world and the next and the authority over both, whose command is effective in the heavens and the earth and all that is in them.
h
The Holy
means the one pure of everything that the polytheists attribute to Him and describe Him with, of what is not among His attributes; the Blessed.
h
The Almighty
means the one severe in His vengeance against His enemies.
h
The Wise
in His governance of His creation and His directing of them in what He knows best of their interests.

x: Commentary on the saying of the Exalted:
h

The likeness of those who were charged with the Torah and then did not carry it out is like the likeness of a donkey carrying volumes. Wretched is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of God. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people (5)
. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says: The likeness of those who were given the Torah, among the Jews and the Christians, and were charged with acting upon it,
h
and then did not carry it out
. He says: then did not act upon what is in it, and denied Muḥammad, peace be upon him, though they were commanded in it to believe in him, follow him and affirm him,
h
is like the likeness of a donkey carrying volumes

. He says: like the donkey that carries on its back books of knowledge, which it does not benefit from and does not understand what is in them. So too those who were given the Torah, in which the matter of Muḥammad, peace be upon him, is made clear: their likeness, when they do not benefit from what is in it, is like the donkey that carries volumes containing knowledge, but it neither understands them nor benefits from them.
The interpreters said about this something like what we have said.

h

. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says to His Prophet Muḥammad, peace be upon him: Say, O Muḥammad, to the Jews:

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, when I asked him about the saying of God:
when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of God

. He said: When you hear the first caller, respond to that, and hurry and do not delay. He said: In the time of the Prophet, peace be upon him, there were only two calls: a call when he sat on the pulpit, and a call when the prayer was begun. He said: This latter one is something that people introduced
afterwards. He said: And trade is not lawful for him when he hears the call that is made in front of the imam when he sits on the pulpit. And he recited:
then hasten to the remembrance of God and leave trade

. He said: He did not command them to leave anything other than it; He forbade trade, then permitted them it again when they finished the prayer. He said: And saʿy is to hurry to it, to turn toward it.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: that in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: "When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of God"

c: It was related to me from al-Ḥusayn, he said:
m: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
then hasten to the remembrance of God

evidence.text: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī told us, from Shuʿbah, he said: Mughīrah informed me, from Ibrāhīm, that it was said to ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him: Ubayy recites it: {hasten}.
ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Bayān al-Sukkarī told us, he said: Sufyān informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father, who said: I never heard ʿUmar recite it other than "proceed" (fa-mḍū) (2).

Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yamān told us, he said: Ḥanẓalah told us, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, he said: ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, used to recite it: "so proceed to the remembrance of God."
Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Ḥanẓalah, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb recited it: "proceed" (fa-mḍū) (3).

Yūnus informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, he said: Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: God took ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may God be pleased with him, and he never recited this verse in which God mentions Friday — {O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday} — except (1) as "proceed to the remembrance of God."

Abū al-Sāʾib told me, he said: Abū Muʿāwiyah told us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, he said: ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd) used to recite it: "proceed to the remembrance of God," and he would say: Had I recited it {hasten}, I would have run until my cloak fell off (2).
He said: This is how he used to recite it.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Azdī told me, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Yamān al-Azdī told us, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī, from al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, that he used to recite it: "proceed to the remembrance of God" (3).
Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yamān told us, he said: Abū Jaʿfar told us, from al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, that he recited it: "proceed to the remembrance of God."
He said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from al-Mughīrah and al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: Had I recited it {hasten}, I would have run until my cloak fell off.
And he used to recite it: "proceed to the remembrance of God" (3).
He said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from al-Shaʿbī, from Ibn Masʿūd, he said: He recited it: "proceed."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, that in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: "When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of God" (3).

x: His saying:
h
and leave trade
. He says: and leave buying and selling when the call is made for the prayer at the time of the sermon.

c: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk used to say about this what Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yamān told us, from Sufyān,
m: , from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, he said: When the sun passes its zenith, buying and selling become forbidden

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk:
m: when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday
. He said: When the sun passes its zenith, buying and selling become forbidden.

c: [Ibn Ḥumayd] told us
m: : Mihrān, from Sufyān, from Ismāʿīl al-Suddī, from Abū Mālik, he said: Some people used to sit in Baqīʿ al-Zubayr, buying and selling when the call was made for prayer on Friday, and not getting up, so there was revealed:
when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday
. As for the remembrance (dhikr) that God, Blessed and Exalted, commanded His believing servants to hasten to, it is the imam's exhortation in his sermon, according to what has been said.

x: Mention of those who said this:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Jābir, from Mujāhid:
m: when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday
. He said: The resolve is at the remembrance, at the sermon.

c: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Ḥanafī told us, he said: ʿAbdān told us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh informed us, he said:
m: Manṣūr, a man of the people of Kūfah, informed us, from Mūsā ibn Abī Kathīr, that he heard Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab say:
when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of God
. He said: It is the imam's exhortation; and when the prayer is finished afterwards

x: His saying:
h
That is better for you, if you only knew

. He says: Your hastening to the remembrance of God when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, and your leaving of trade, is better for you than buying and selling at that time, if you know what is good and harmful for yourselves. The reciters differed in how to read His saying:
h
on the day of al-Jumuʿah
. The majority of the reciters of the major cities read
h
al-Jumuʿah
with a ḍammah on the mīm and the jīm, except al-Aʿmash, who read it with the mīm vowelless
n
. The correct reading, in our view, is what the reciters of the major cities follow, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in how to read His saying: {on the day of al-Jumuʿah}.
The majority of the reciters of the major cities read {al-Jumuʿah} with a ḍammah on the mīm and the jīm, except al-Aʿmash, who read it with the mīm vowelless (1).
The correct reading, in our view, is what the reciters of the major cities follow, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

x: Commentary on the saying of the Exalted:
h
And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse through the land and seek of the bounty of God, and remember God often that you may succeed (10)
. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says: When the Friday prayer has been concluded on the day of Friday, disperse through the land if you wish — a concession from God to you in that.
The interpreters said about this something like what we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm told me, he said: Hushaym told us, he said: Ḥuṣayn informed us, from Mujāhid, that he said:
m: It is a concession. He means His saying:
And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse through the land

c: It was related to me from al-Ḥusayn, he said:
m: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse through the land
. He said: This is a permission from God; whoever wishes may go out, and whoever wishes may stay seated.

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: He permitted them, when they finished the prayer, and said:
And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse through the land and seek of the bounty of God
— I have made it lawful for you.

x: His saying:
h
and seek of the bounty of God
Something was reported from the Prophet, peace be upon him, in the interpretation of that, as al-ʿAbbās ibn Abī Ṭālib told me, he said:

c: ʿAlī ibn al-Muʿāfā ibn Yaʿqūb al-Mawṣilī told us, he said:
m: from Mosul told us, from Abū Khalaf, from Anas, he said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said regarding His saying:
And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse through the land and seek of the bounty of God
: "It is not for seeking worldly gain, but for visiting a sick person, attending a funeral, and visiting a brother for the sake of God"
and seek of the bounty of God
may also be understood to mean: and seek from the bounty of God, in whose hand are the keys of His treasuries, for your world and your Hereafter.
b.via: ʿAlī ibn al-Muʿāfā ibn Yaʿqūb al-Mawṣilī

x: His saying:
h
and remember God often that you may succeed

. He says: and remember God often by praising Him and thanking Him for what He has favored you with of success in performing His obligations, that you may succeed, attain what you seek with your Lord, and reach eternity in His Gardens.
Commentary on the saying of the Exalted:
h

But when they saw a transaction of trade or some amusement, they rushed to it and left you standing. Say: What is with God is better than amusement and than trade; and God is the best of providers (11)
. The Exalted, Mighty be His mention, says: When the believers saw a caravan of trade or some amusement,
h
they rushed to it
. That is, they hurried to the trade,
h
and left you standing

. He says to the Prophet, peace be upon him: and they left you, O Muḥammad, standing on the pulpit. That is because the trade they saw, to which the people rushed, leaving the Prophet, peace be upon him, standing, was oil that Diḥyah ibn Khalīfah had brought from Syria.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Ismāʿīl al-Suddī, from Abū Mālik, he said:
m: Diḥyah ibn Khalīfah came from Syria with a trade of oil while the Prophet, peace be upon him, was giving the sermon on Friday. When they saw him, they got up and went to him at al-Baqīʿ, fearing that they would be beaten to it. He said: So there was revealed:
But when they saw a transaction of trade or some amusement, they rushed to it and left you standing

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yamān told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from al-Suddī,
m: when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday

. He said: Diḥyah al-Kalbī came with a trade while the Prophet, peace be upon him, was standing in the prayer on Friday, so they left the Prophet, peace be upon him, and went out to him, and there was revealed:
But when they saw a transaction of trade or some amusement, they rushed to it and left you standing
until the end of the surah (1).

c: Abū Ḥaṣīn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Yūnus told me, he said: ʿAbthar told us, he said: Ḥuṣayn told us, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, he said:
m: We were with the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, at the Friday prayer when a caravan carrying food passed by. He said: The people went out except twelve men, and the verse of Friday was revealed

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, he said: al-Ḥasan said:
m: The people of Medina were afflicted with hunger and high prices, then a caravan arrived while the Prophet, peace be upon him, was giving the sermon on Friday. They heard of it and went out while the Prophet, peace be upon him, was standing, as God, Mighty and Majestic, said

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: But when they saw a transaction of trade or some amusement, they rushed to it and left you standing
. He said: A trade came, so they went off to it and left the Prophet, peace be upon him, standing; and when they see amusement and play, say:
What is with God is better than amusement and than trade; and God is the best of providers

c: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying:
But when they saw a transaction of trade or some amusement, they rushed to it
. He said: Men who used to rise to their water-carrying camels

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: While the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, was giving a sermon to the people on Friday, they began to slip away and get up until only a small band of them remained. He said: "How many are you?" They counted themselves, and there were twelve men and a woman. Then he stood up on the second Friday and began to address them. Sufyān said: And I only know that in his report is: and he exhorted them and reminded them. Again they began to slip away and get up until a small band remained, and he said: "How many are you?" They counted themselves

, and there were twelve men and a woman. Then he stood up on the third Friday, and they began to slip away and get up until a small band of them remained, and he said: "How many are you?" They counted themselves, and there were twelve men and a woman. He said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, if the last of you had followed the first of you, the valley would have blazed with fire over you." And God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:
But when they saw a transaction of trade or some amusement, they rushed to it

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: they rushed to it and left you standing
. He said: If the last of them had followed the first of them, the valley would have blazed with fire over them
. He said: Ibn Thawr told us, he said: Maʿmar said: Qatādah said: Nothing remained with the Prophet, peace be upon him, that day except twelve men, and a woman with them (3).

c: Muḥammad ibn ʿUmārah al-Rāzī told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ told us, he said: Hushaym told us, he said: Ḥuṣayn informed us, from Sālim and Abū Sufyān, from Jābir,
m: . He said: A caravan arrived, and they rushed to it, and nothing remained with the Prophet, peace be upon him, except twelve men

c: ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-Āmulī told us, he said: Jarīr told us, from Ḥuṣayn, from Sālim, from Jābir,
m: that the Prophet, peace be upon him, used to give the sermon standing on Friday, and a caravan came from Syria, and the people turned to it until only twelve men remained. He said: So this verse was revealed concerning "Friday":
But when they saw a transaction of trade or some amusement, they rushed to it and left you standing
. As for the amusement, there is disagreement about which kind of amusement it was.

x: Some said: It was a drum (kabar)
n
and pipes.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muḥammad ibn Sahl ibn ʿAskar told us, he said: Yaḥyā ibn Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Sulaymān ibn Bilāl told us, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, he said:
m: When girls were married, people would pass by with the drum and the pipes, leaving the Prophet, peace be upon him, standing on the pulpit and rushing to them, so God revealed:
But when they saw a transaction of trade or some amusement, they rushed to it

x: Others said: It was a drum (ṭabl).
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, he said: The amusement is the drum

c: Al-Ḥārith told me, he said:
m: told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ mentioned, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Bakr, from Mujāhid, that the amusement is the drum. The view that is more correct on this is the report that we related from Jābir, because he witnessed the affair of the people

x: His saying:
h
Say: What is with God is better than amusement and than trade

. The One whose praise is majestic says to His Prophet Muḥammad, peace be upon him: Say to them, O Muḥammad: What is with God of reward, for the one who sits listening to the sermon of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and his exhortation on Friday until the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, finishes it, is better for him than the amusement and the trade to which they rush,
h
and God is the best of providers

. He says: God is the best of providers, so seek Him in the pursuit of your livelihoods, and ask Him alone to expand His bounty for you, and not anyone else. End of the commentary on Surah "al-Jumu'ah".

notes.en: Reported by Abū ʿUbayd in Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān pp. 185–186 and Ibn Abī Shaybah 2/157 via Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, from Kharashah; Ibn Ḥajar declared this chain sound in al-Fatḥ 8/642. Al-Suyūṭī, in al-Durr al-manthūr 6/219, attributes it to Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn al-Anbārī in al-Maṣāḥif. The reading "fa-mḍū" is anomalous (shādhdh) because it contradicts the script of the codex (muṣḥaf). Perhaps it belongs to what had its recitation abrogated, or was before the final review (ʿarḍah), or is among what the consensus was to abandon, since the Companions agreed to follow the codex of ʿUthmān.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو عبيد في فضائل القرآن ص 185، 186، وابن أبي شيبة 2/ 157 من طريق مغيرة عن إبراهيم عن خرشة، وصحح ابن حجر هذا الإسناد في الفتح 8/ 642. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 219 إلى سعيد بن منصور وابن المنذر وابن الأنباري في المصاحف. وقراءة: (فامضوا) شاذة لمخالفتها رسم المصحف. ولعلها مما نُسخت تلاوته، أو كان قبل العَرضة الأخيرة، أو مما انعقد الإجماع على تركه؛ لإجماع الصحابة على اتباع مصحف عثمان.

notes.en: Reported by al-Shāfiʿī in al-Umm 1/196, al-Dāraquṭnī in al-ʿIlal 2/253 (253), Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah 9/29 and al-Bayhaqī 3/227 via Sufyān with this chain. ʿAbd al-Razzāq reported it in al-Muṣannaf (5348) via al-Zuhrī with this chain — and he has it in the Tafsīr 2/291 with the same chain as a recitation of Ibn ʿUmar — and Mālik 1/106 reported from al-Zuhrī: ʿUmar used to recite [text unclear in source]. Al-Suyūṭī, in al-Durr al-manthūr 6/219, attributes it to al-Firyābī, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn al-Anbārī in al-Maṣāḥif.
